newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Friday, Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Friday, Jan 24.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- SIB HEAD SURPRISES CITY WITH DECISION TO STEP DOWN

The chief regulator of the City of London, Sir Andrew Large of the Securities and Investments Board, has unexpectedly announced that he will not accept reappointment to a second term. The move adds to uncertainty over the future of City regulation with the Labour party promising that a Labour government would fold the three self-regulatory organisations that oversee City companies into the SIB.
-- POST MANAGERS ATTACK PLANS TO CURB STRIKES

The government faces a further deterioration in its relations with business after proposing more curbs on public sector strikes. The Confederation of British Industry will next week publish its response to the plans, and it is expected to be critical. Post Office managers have also criticised the proposals and the Institute of Management has urged the government to drop the plans.
-- POUND PLUNGES AS EXPECTATIONS OF RATE RISE RECEDE

The pound fell sharply against the US dollar and the German Deutschemark on Thursday following a lowering of expectations in financial markets of a pre-election interest rate rise. The pound has risen by 13 percent against a basket of currencies since last August, and the downward movement will be welcomed by hard-hit exporters. Weak economic data over the past two weeks has persuaded the money markets a rate rise is not expected.
-- VAT RULING COULD HAND HEALTH GROUPS MILLIONS

The Court of Appeal has overturned a High Court decision on VAT payable on drugs and some surgical appliances. The ruling means that private hospitals are set to reclaim tens of millions of pounds paid in VAT for medical supplies they purchased for patients. Customs and Excise is to seek leave to appeal to the House of Lords on the issue, which has been running since 1992.
-- INDUSTRY BACKS CLARKE ON RATES

The latest survey from the British Chambers of Commerce has added support to Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's policy of keeping interest rates unchanged. The survey, released Thursday, showed manufacturing growth in the final quarter of 1996 was reigned in by the sharp rise in sterling. The findings echo those of the CBI earlier this week, which also supported the policy of resisting calls from the Bank of England to raise rates in order to cool the economy.
-- NEW OPPOSITION TO BIG SIX MOVE

The British Venture Capital Association has called on the Office of Fair Trading to refuse an accord filed late last year by the Big Six accountancy firms. The association claims the measure, which would impose a limit on the legal liability of accountancy firms when they give negligent advice on investment deals, amounts to a cartel that will restrict competition.
-- FORD WORKERS TO HOLD STRIKE VOTE OVER CUTS

Ford Motor Co is facing a nationwide strike in the UK over its plan to cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant in Merseyside. The strike vote by 30,000 workers comes after talks failed to change Ford's plan to reduce the production of the Escort model at Halewood. Unions say it is the most serious industrial dispute to hit Ford in the UK in the past decade.
-- 80M STG WILLIAM COOK BUY-OUT PLANNED

The management of steel castings group William Cook has unexpectedly announced it is planning an 80 million stg MBO, following a 10-week takeover battle for the group involving rival castings group Triplex Lloyd. The MBO is backed by venture capital group Electra Fleming.
-- SEGA PLANS MERGER WITH BANDAI

Japanese electronic games maker Sega plans to merge with toy company Bandai to create one of the world's largest multimedia entertainment groups. The deal would give the new venture annual sales of over Y600 bn (three bn stg) and combined assets of $589 bn, and is to be completed on October 1. The move would let the groups pool distribution and reduce corporate overhead.
-- PEPTIDE AND MEDEVA LINK TESTS POSITIVE

Peptide Therapeutics, the biotechnology company, saw its shares rise 47.5p to 289p on Thursday following news that pharmaceutical group Medeva has taken a three percent stake in the company and has agreed to collaborate on new-style vaccines. Shares in Medeva, which paid three million stg for the stake, rose 8.5p to 288p on the news, as well as positive test results for two products in development.
